archive_note: Per-source evidence_checked_at and vendor_profiles define what was rechecked. Historical LLNL, MUSA, preview and research records retain their prior dates unless explicitly revisited. Product mechanism evidence, package support and target-GPU execution are separate; the self-developed target remains GPU_NOT_RUN.

vendor_profiles.version_baseline: Compute Sanitizer release notes 2026.3 (updated 2026-09-09); CUDA Toolkit 13.4 NVCC manual; compiler memcheck introduced with CUDA 13.1
hardware_requirements: Compute Sanitizer 2026.3 lists CUDA GPUs with SM 7.5 and above, with compatible driver/toolkit
Instruction-specific and compile-time shared-memory coverage still depends on architecture and release
instrumentation: Default memcheck uses runtime binary instrumentation and current-address/allocation checks
NVCC/PTXAS compile-time memcheck performs original-object base-and-bounds analysis when it succeeds; fallback checks do not preserve a proven original-object guarantee
Public material does not expose the complete private compiler pass or metadata ABI; a self-developed LLVM D1 implementation is a project design choice
runtime_requirements: Compiler tools including standalone PTX compiler libraries and Compute Sanitizer must come from the same Toolkit version
Compiler-instrumented binaries must run under compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck; running directly or under another checker is unsupported
JIT compile-time patching uses the release-note-specific -Xptxas=-sanitize=memcheck path
detector_scope: memcheck global/local/shared device memory and supported allocation diagnostics
initcheck default global; shared/all selectable in documented versions
racecheck shared-memory data hazards, and synccheck supported synchronization misuse
known_limitations: Only memcheck supports compile-time instrumentation; racecheck/initcheck/synccheck remain separate runtime checks
Function-level hybrid inside one module is unsupported; uninstrumented functions in such a module will not be binary instrumented
NV-C HMM is unsupported and can produce false positives; compile-time shared accesses with clusters are also restricted
2026.3 adds shared outer-boundary checks on Hopper and newer but still lists missed overflows between shared variables in the same allocation
Runtime/current-address checks do not guarantee A-derived accesses landing inside live B are detected
Extra register/stack and tracking memory can prevent launches; no detected error is not evidence that every launch was checked

vendor_profiles.version_baseline: ROCm 7.2.4 pinned GPU ASan mechanism/limitations; ROCm 10.1.0 release 2026-10-05 and versioned ASAN package/setup requirements; LLNL 7.0.0 and 7.13.0 preview remain separate historical evidence
hardware_requirements: Official GPU ASan requires a supported xnack+ configuration and Linux HMM; HSA_XNACK=1 cannot create missing hardware or virtualization support
ROCm 10.1 prebuilt ASAN packages are limited to gfx942, gfx950 and an all build containing both
The older gfx90a:xnack+ example is not a supported-architecture claim for the 10.1 package set
instrumentation: LLVM/Clang device memory instrumentation with GPU-visible Shadow/Poison/Redzone metadata
Software Shadow checks use GPU instructions; absence of a special Shadow ISA instruction does not invalidate an independently implemented checker
runtime_requirements: 7.2.4 mechanism guide uses -fsanitize=address -shared-libsan with ASan-enabled HIP/HSA libraries and the ASan host runtime
10.1 packages install separately in /opt/rocm/core-asan-10.1 and retain HMM, HSA_XNACK=1 and instrumented-runtime setup requirements
A self-developed no-XNACK B2 must premap, initialize, publish and retain readable Shadow metadata; it is not the official ROCm supported configuration
detector_scope: Supported GPU device addressability and memory-error reports for instrumented accesses
Lifetime/poison checks within published Shadow state and officially supported memory spaces
known_limitations: The 7.2.4 mechanism guide warns unsupported offload targets can generate runnable but uninstrumented device code
The 7.2.4 guide lists uninstrumented Private/Stack, LDS modeled as Global, finite Redzone escapes and faults on wild-pointer Shadow reads
Do not infer all older Known Issues are unchanged in 10.1 from package installation documentation alone
XNACK retries recoverable faults but does not automatically supply correct Poison state for arbitrary addresses

vendor_profiles.version_baseline: Intel DPC++/C++ 2026.2 guide dated 2026-10-15; compiler 2026.2.0 released 2026-10-22; 2026.0 records retained as history; UR specification is independently maintained
hardware_requirements: The official 2026.2 guide documents Linux with one Intel Ponte Vecchio GPU card
Level Zero GPU selection and SYCL versus OpenMP runtime setup use distinct documented instructions
instrumentation: ASan combines compiler instrumentation and UR/libdevice Shadow mapping, making it a B2-type product reference rather than an additional spatial reference configuration
The public support table does not establish D1 original-object or D2 generation guarantees
runtime_requirements: SYCL uses its documented Level Zero selector; Intel 2026.2 OpenMP examples use the unified_runtime plugin and explicit matching UR_ENABLE_LAYERS
Generic UR guidance delegates layer enabling to the language runtime; do not merge it with product commands into a universal adapter recipe
Compatible compiler, language runtime, Unified Runtime, driver and GPU configuration
detector_scope: ASan supports documented global/USM/local/private memory errors and SYCL-specific buffer/context/free checks
MSan device uninitialized-use checks; TSan documented device USM race detection
known_limitations: Device ASan forces kernels into sequential execution, changing concurrency semantics
Large workgroup counts may skip ASan Local/Private OOB or MSan Local/Private uninitialized-use checks
Device private-memory overhead can reduce permitted workgroup size
UR specification planned labels and auto-enable guidance do not imply uniform MSan/TSan support or identical setup across adapters

vendor_profiles.version_baseline: MUSA published v1.1.1 guide/release note; undated portions not assigned an invented release date
hardware_requirements: Follow explicit version-specific MUSA and driver hardware support tables; do not generalize an MTT S5000 example to all devices
instrumentation: Public documentation describes a GPU runtime debugging tool; internal machine-code/Shadow/provenance algorithm remains undisclosed
runtime_requirements: Matching mt-compute-sanitizer and supported MUSA runtime/driver environment
detector_scope: Publicly documented device global out-of-bounds and API-return-error checks
Memory leak detection requires the separately enabled leak-check mode
known_limitations: Current published descriptions do not establish complete private/shared/local/host-pinned coverage
Some atomic/special LSU paths are not established as supported in the cited guide
No evidence establishes equivalence to NV-R binary rewriting, AMD-B2 Shadow or NV-C original-object analysis
